question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [French Naval Bases and Settlements in India]
wrong_fact: Karaikal is located on the Coromandel Coast (modern-day Puducherry UT/Tamil Nadu region) of southeastern India, NOT the Konkan Coast (which is on the western coast of India).
explanation: Pondicherry (Coromandel Coast), Chandernagore (Bengal), and Mahe (Malabar Coast) are all correctly matched to their geographic regions. Karaikal was established as a French settlement/base on the Coromandel Coast in 1739 after purchasing it from the Raja of Tanjore, not on the western Konkan Coast.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Key French Naval Stations/Islands and their Strategic Roles]
options: Île de France (Mauritius) — Primary French naval base and staging ground in the Indian Ocean
Bourbon (Réunion) — Agricultural supply base for the French fleet
Diego Garcia — Main operational headquarters of Admiral d'Aché's squadron
Mahé (Seychelles) — Transit point and provisioning station between East Africa and India
wrong_fact: Diego Garcia was not the main operational headquarters of Admiral d'Aché's squadron; the squadron operated out of the fortified base at Île de France (Mauritius) and Pondicherry during the Seven Years' War.
explanation: Île de France (Mauritius) served as the primary naval dockyard and headquarters for the French Indian Ocean fleet under Bertrand-François Mahé de La Bourdonnais and later Admiral d'Aché. Bourbon (Réunion) supplied the fleet with grain and provisions. Mahé in the Seychelles was named after La Bourdonnais and served as a strategic transit stop. Diego Garcia was not occupied or used as a headquarters by the French fleet during these confrontations.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [French Naval Engagements and the Locations of Confrontation]
options: Battle of Madras (1746) — Capture of Fort St. George on the Coromandel Coast by La Bourdonnais
Battle of Sadras (1758) — First naval clash of the Seven Years' War off the coast of Madras
Battle of Negapatam (1782) — Indecisive engagement between Suffren and Hughes off the Tamil Nadu coast
Battle of Providien (1782) — Clash between Suffren and Hughes off the coast of Malabar
wrong_fact: The Battle of Providien (April 1782) was fought off the eastern coast of Ceylon (Sri Lanka) near the islet of Providien, NOT off the coast of Malabar (western India).
explanation: The naval campaign between Admiral Suffren (French) and Vice-Admiral Edward Hughes (British) was fought entirely in the Bay of Bengal and waters around Ceylon. The Battle of Providien occurred near Trincomalee on the east coast of Ceylon, not the Malabar Coast. The other battles: Madras (1746), Sadras (1758), and Negapatam (1782) are correctly matched to the Coromandel/Tamil Nadu coast.
